title: introduce-presubmit-registry-and-dep-curation-api
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add: presubmit registry service and dependency curation HTTP API; Change: split presubmit profiles into team-aware slices and introduce lightweight adapter for staged releases; Fix: reduce presubmit startup latency via on-demand plugin hydration.
description: Motivation: Teams running presubmit checks have diverged needs (language, test weight, infra quotas). Our current monolithic presubmit config makes incremental CI optimization and targeted caching hard. This PR scaffolds a lightweight presubmit-registry service + an opinionated dep-curation API so teams can register small, composable presubmit profiles that the CI executor hydrates on-demand. Goals: 1) Reduce presubmit startup time for small changes by hydrating only relevant profiles; 2) Enable per-team dependency scoping to improve cache hit rates and allow safe dev-dep rotation; 3) Provide a stable HTTP API so other repos (sdk, docs, examples) can opt into staged presubmit behavior without copying manifests. Summary of changes: - New service: infra/presubmit-registry (small Go service + compact manifest store). - API: POST /v1/profiles/resolve (returns merged presubmit profile for a commit/paths signature). - CLI shim: tools/presubmit-client (TS) used by GitHub Actions to resolve profiles at job start. - CI workflows: small updates to .github/workflows/presubmit-*.yml to call the registry early and conditionally run lint/test shards. - Presubmit profiles: migrated existing team profiles into registry manifests under infra/presubmit-registry/manifests/* - Dep curation: introduced a mechanism to annotate devdeps with "curation tags" in manifest to enable lightweight pruning and cache partitioning. Commits: - a2f7d4f: add presubmit registry scaffold and manifest loader - b8c4e1c: implement /v1/profiles/resolve and local cache - 9f3b1aa: add presubmit-client CLI and GH Action step - 4d2e8b0: migrate team profiles and update workflows - 7c11a9d: docs and examples for registry API usage Changed files (high-level): - infra/presubmit-registry/main.go (new) - infra/presubmit-registry/manifest_loader.go (new) - infra/presubmit-registry/manifests/team-*.yaml (new) - tools/presubmit-client/src/index.ts (new) - .github/workflows/presubmit-node.yml (modified) - .github/workflows/presubmit-python.yml (modified) - docs/dev/presubmit-registry.md (new) - ci/ci-runner/presubmit_adapter.go (modified) - scripts/dep-curator/annotate_devdeps.py (new) - scripts/presubmit/bootstrap.sh (removed) Design notes: - Registry is intentionally minimal: manifests are declarative and immutable by default (versioned by sha). We expect the control plane to be lightweight and to rely on Git for audits. - Resolution algorithm: merge global base -> team slice -> path overrides with last-wins semantics for shard weights. - Security: registry accepts signed resolution requests from the GH Action runner (short-lived token) and enforces a read-only manifest store. No write API is exposed in this PR. Testing/QA: - Unit tests for resolver and manifest loader included (infra/presubmit-registry/*_test.go). - E2E smoke in a new workflow .github/workflows/presubmit-smoke.yml that runs against a staged manifest set. - Local dev flow: tools/presubmit-client supports --local-manifest for offline dev. Rollout plan: - Canary: enable the registry in the main repo for non-critical presubmit lanes (lint fastpath) for 48h. - Observability: presubmit-registry exposes metrics (resolution_latencies, cache_hit_ratio) and traces. We will add alerting if resolution latency > 2s for >1% of requests. - Migration: teams can opt-in by moving manifests; fallback to legacy presubmit if registry is unreachable. CI summary: - Initial CI run failed due to flaky network check in the GH Action step; fixed by increasing timeout and adding retry logic (2 retries). - Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, e2e-smoke). "Full CI matrix: unit-go (pass), unit-ts (pass), lint (pass), e2e-smoke (pass)" Review thread: - Liam: "Nice separation — can we make the manifest merge deterministic if two team slices overlap?" Maya: "Yes — last-wins by manifest ordering; added explicit note and a small helper to fail on ambiguous full overrides." - Priya: "Do we need per-team RBAC for the registry?" Maya: "Not in this iteration; registry is read-only and manifest changes flow through git-based PRs. We'll add RBAC when admin UI is introduced." - Diego: "Can we gate presubmit client on a feature flag so we can switch back quickly?" Maya: "Added GH Action input presubmit_registry_enabled with fallback to legacy step." Post-review changes included: - tighten resolve semantics to be deterministic - add retry+backoff for HTTP calls in GH Action - add metrics and expose /metrics Prometheus endpoint Merge decision: approved by reviewers after addressing comments. Merge method: squash and merge. Notes on repo hygiene: - Removed duplicate team profiles from ci/profiles/* (addresses drift). - Small tidy: remove legacy presubmit bootstrap script that was unused (scripts/presubmit/bootstrap.sh). Potential follow-ups: - Add a write API with RBAC for self-serve manifest publishing (ENG-1893) - Implement manifest diff-based presubmit warm-up to further reduce cold start time - Expand dep-curation hooks to support quantized lockfile generation Known limitations: - Registry does not yet implement strong auth for non-GH runners; documented as an action item. - The per-profile shard weighting is coarse; we will iterate with telemetry. Overall this PR is a refactor/feature hybrid: it reorganizes presubmit configuration into a small service + thin CI client with the aim of improving presubmit performance, reducing duplication, and enabling safer dependency curation.
